title: Ecco: Improving Memory Bandwidth and Capacity for LLMs via Entropy-Aware Cache Compression
problem: LLM inference is severely memory-bandwidth-bound and memory-capacity-constrained due to large KV caches and weight tensors; the KV cache alone can consume 72.7% of GPU memory. Existing quantization schemes (AWQ, SmoothQuant, Quarot) reduce storage but introduce high runtime decompression overheads that negate bandwidth savings or compromise accuracy.
motivation: As LLM decode is inherently memory-bound (low arithmetic intensity GEMV-dominated), cache-level lossy compression that operates transparently on the HBM-to-L2 data path can directly multiply effective bandwidth and capacity without altering compute kernels.
method: Ecco places compressors/decompressors between a GPU's fast cache and main memory. It compresses weights and KV cache to 1/4 their size by grouping 128 values and replacing each group with the nearest match from 64 learned patterns (k-means: selecting the closest representative value), then applies Huffman coding with 4 codebooks per pattern for further compression (using shorter codes for common values); activations use simpler 2x INT8 compression. The decompressor runs 64 parallel Huffman decoders on overlapping 15-bit chunks of 512-bit blocks, feeding results into a 6-stage tree circuit and 128 parallel mappers. The compressor uses a bitonic sorter to extract outliers and scores 16 candidate patterns to pick the best one, with both components replicated 20x to sustain the cache's 5,120 bytes/cycle throughput, in 28nm silicon (scalable to 7nm).
key_novelty: The core innovation is a parallel Huffman decoder with 64 overlapping sub-decoders fused into a tree-combining stage that breaks the sequential bottleneck of normal Huffman decoding, achieving 100x latency reduction while maintaining GPU L2 cache speed for a lossy entropy-aware compression scheme.
contributions: Entropy-aware cache compression scheme combining group-wise non-uniform k-means quantization with shared patterns and Huffman coding, achieving 4x memory capacity expansion for LLM weights and KV cache.
Parallel Huffman-based decoder with 64 concurrent sub-decoders and 6-stage tree concatenation, reducing decoding latency by 100x vs. sequential Huffman.
Efficient 4x compressor using bitonic sorter and min/max k-means fitness scoring for online KV cache compression with negligible accuracy impact.
End-to-end evaluation demonstrating 2.9x speedup over AWQ, 2.4x over Olive accelerator, and nearly 4x capacity increase on A100 GPU, with <1% chip area overhead (5.11 mm2 on 826 mm2 die).

metrics.speedup: 2.9x over TensorRT FP16 (avg), 2.9x over AWQ, 2.4x over Olive, 1.9x over SmoothQuant on LLaMA-13B decode
metrics.area: 5.11 mm2 total hardware addition on A100 (826 mm2 die), <1% area overhead; 7.36 W power (<10% of A100 idle power)
metrics.accuracy: LLaMA2-7B perplexity 5.65 (W4A8KV4) vs AWQ 5.83; outperforms all baselines on LLaMA/LLaMA2 7B-70B
metrics.other: 4x memory capacity enlargement for weights and KV cache; 2x for activations

limitations: Simulation validated only up to 4K sequence length due to slow simulation speed; KV cache online compression uses a simplified min/max pattern selector (16 patterns) rather than the offline MSE-optimal 64-pattern search, potentially reducing compression efficiency.
primary_theme: entropy-aware cache compression for LLM inference on GPU
